llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed multi-model review tool, but it can send full sensitive designs to external model services and exposes a public session-sharing capability without strong built-in safeguards.

dimensions.detail: Network use and a mumo API key are expected for a multi-provider deliberation service, but the scope is broad because OpenClaw exposes all eight MCP tools by default and the skill encourages use on sensitive security and business material.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is manual and disclosed through OpenClaw skill installation or git clone, with a separate manual MCP server registration pointing to https://mumo.chat/api/mcp. The chmod 600 and .env guidance is credential-hygiene documentation, not root escalation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The playbooks instruct the agent to include full specs, API surfaces, auth flows, launch plans, and pricing models, while the skill is especially triggered for auth, security, tokens, payments, and data exposure. The artifacts do not require explicit user confirmation, redaction, or data minimization before remote submission.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent OpenClaw MCP configuration and stores the API key in ~/.openclaw/.env, and the remote service keeps recoverable sessions via list_sessions/get_session. This is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users should understand the remote retention and public-sharing implications.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core purpose is coherent: create mumo deliberation sessions, wait for model responses, append follow-up rounds, and synthesize results. The concern is that the enabled tool set also includes share_session, which can publish session content at a public link and is not required for ordinary deliberation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending review prompts and included specs to mumo and potentially multiple external model providers. Before using it on auth flows, tokens, payment systems, customer data, or unreleased security findings, require the agent to minimize excerpts, redact secrets, and ask before transmitting or sharing sessions publicly.
llm.findings:
[T09] expected: Remote prompt transmission to mumo and downstream model providers is central to the skill, but the artifact-backed concern remains: design-review and red-team playbooks direct full sensitive materials into prompts without mandatory consent, redaction, or minimization.
[T05] unexpected: The share_session tool is documented and not hidden, but public sharing is not necessary for the core create/wait/read/append workflow and no default allowlist or explicit per-call confirmation gate is documented.
[PE3] expected: The .env reference is for storing the user's mumo API key outside the MCP config; the README explicitly recommends restrictive permissions and avoiding shell-history exposure, so this is credential hygiene rather than evidence of theft.
[PE2] expected: The chmod 600 command restricts the user's own .env file and does not invoke sudo or root privileges; this scanner concern is downgraded.
[RA2] expected: The session and takeaway references are part of normal remote deliberation state and recovery; I found no cron job, startup hook, or local backdoor persistence in the artifacts.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger scope is broad and includes security-sensitive pre-implementation reviews, but that matches the stated purpose. The concern is not invocation breadth alone; it compounds with remote submission of sensitive content.
[TM3] expected: The cited world-readable language warns against unsafe permissions and recommends chmod 600 before adding the key, so it is a protective default rather than an unsafe one.
[EA2] expected: The autonomy preference example relates to appending deliberation rounds and model selection, not destructive local actions. The skill also tells the agent to align with the user on whether to append a round.
